newsitem.title: FRANCE: French strikes hit flights, rail traffic.
newsitem.headline: French strikes hit flights, rail traffic.

text.p: Striking pilots and cabin crew at French units of British Airways voted on Saturday to suspend a 17-day strike and rail traffic was also returning to normal after a strike by conductors.
Unions at British Airways' TAT and Air Liberte agreed to resume work from midday on Sunday after winning concessions from management on pay and conditions, they said in a statement.
They said they would continue to push for an improved deal by other means. The strike forced cancellation of about a quarter of Saturday's planned flights.
Flights were also disrupted on Saturday at British Airway's rival Air France Europe, which cancelled 55 percent of its mostly domestic schedule on the second and final day of a pilots' strike.
The Air France Europe pilots have staged a string of stoppages to protest at cuts in their pay and what they say are unacceptable working conditions in a merger with parent Air France.
Meanwhile, SNCF state railways said traffic was getting back to normal after lingering strikes by conductors, who originally called a 36-hour stoppage ending on Friday morning.
Workers in Clermont-Ferrand and in south-east Paris, among the most militant, voted a return to work.
Their strikes had disrupted services including high-speed trains leaving Paris for the south. Regional services around Toulouse were still hit by lingering strikes.
"We are getting back to a normal traffic on the main lines, including high speed trains," a SNCF spokesman said.
The conductors are pushing for higher wages, running against the grain of austerity cuts decreed by the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
The strikes are a reminder of the power of French unions in France as it prepares for a parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.
